onboarding.intro.title: Take a quick tour
onboarding.intro.body: Explore the main sections in a few clicks. You can reopen this guide from Help whenever you need a reminder.
onboarding.convert.title: Convert
onboarding.convert.body: Choose a preset, upload video or image media, tune size/FPS settings, run conversion, then preview or download GIF outputs.
onboarding.patch.title: Patch Tools
onboarding.patch.body: Patch existing GIF files without rerunning conversion, including EOF byte and header width/height fixes.
onboarding.steam.title: Steam Helpers
onboarding.steam.body: Copy a script that uploads your GIFs to Steam as Workshop, Artwork or Screenshot items, with step-by-step help for the browser Console.
onboarding.guides.title: Guides
onboarding.guides.body: Use built-in workflow notes when you forget which preset, patch, or upload path matches a Steam artwork task.
feedback.title: Did the result work for you?
feedback.body: Your GIFs are ready. If anything looked off, or a preset worked well, tell us on the Steam guide - it is the fastest way to get it fixed.
convert.title: Media to GIF
convert.intro: Encode source media into Steam-specific layouts with control over frame rate, size ceilings, retries, and post-processing patches.

convert.cutPreview.title: Cut Preview
convert.cutPreview.summary: Scaled to {size} px, cut into {count, plural, one {# GIF} other {# GIFs}}
convert.cutPreview.summaryGuide: Center {size} px square; the shaded area is trimmed
convert.cutPreview.rowsNote: Row heights may shift slightly during conversion if one row needs more room to fit the size limit.
convert.cutPreview.unavailable: Your browser can't display this file, so there is no preview. It can still be converted.
convert.cutPreview.realSizeHint: Shown at the real size of the GIFs. Click the preview to crop or trim the source.
convert.editor.title: Edit source
convert.editor.bodyVideo: Drag the box or its handles to crop, and set the start and end to trim. Only the edited part is converted.
convert.editor.bodyImage: Drag the box or its handles to crop. Only the cropped area is converted.
convert.longMp4Memo.title: Long MP4 guidance
convert.longMp4Memo.body: For MP4 files over 20 seconds, Workshop with 3 rows usually gives the best result because motion is spread across more GIFs. If the source is nearly static, 1 row may still be enough.
convert.memoryMemo.title: High memory use
convert.memoryMemo.body: 3-row Workshop conversions can use about 4GB RAM for short MP4s and up to 16GB for long, high-motion clips. Use 1 row unless you need the taller showcase grid.
convert.rawModeActive: Raw mode active: FPS/quality retries and max-size limit are ignored.
convert.rawModeInactive: Use raw mode when you want original encode behavior without optimization constraints.
convert.shadowDarkening.note: Turns near-black areas pure black to remove grainy noise in dark parts of the GIF. Often makes the file smaller too.
convert.optimizationInactive: Optimization controls are inactive because Disable Optimizations is on.
convert.retriesNeedStandard: FPS/Quality reduction toggles activate after enabling standard retries.
convert.lossyOn: Lossy mode can reduce quality and apply extra compression passes after standard optimization.
convert.lossyOff: Lossy mode is off. Only standard optimization passes will run.

steam.title: Steam Upload Helpers
steam.intro: Small scripts that fill in Steam's upload form for you. They run in your own browser, on Steam's page, with your existing Steam sign-in.
steam.paste.title: Before you paste: type allow pasting
steam.paste.body: The first time you paste into the DevTools Console, Chrome, Edge and Firefox block it and ask you to type allow pasting. Type it, press Enter, then paste the script again. This is a guard against scams, not an error, and you only do it once per browser.
steam.paste.safety: Only paste code you can read in full, and only on steamcommunity.com. Every script on this page is shown under “View script”.
steam.run.title: How to run a script
steam.run.open: Sign in to Steam in your browser and open the upload page.
steam.run.console: Open the Console: press <kbd>F12</kbd> (<kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>Option</kbd>+<kbd>I</kbd> on a Mac) and choose the Console tab.
steam.run.allow: First time only: type allow pasting and press Enter.
steam.run.paste: Copy one script below, paste it into the Console and press <kbd>Enter</kbd>.
steam.type.workshop.desc: Workshop parts. They appear in your profile's Workshop showcase.
steam.type.featured.desc: Featured GIFs and the 506 + 100 Artwork Showcase split, uploaded as long artwork.
steam.type.screenshot.desc: The same long images, uploaded as screenshots instead.
steam.effect.workshop: Marks each upload as a Workshop item (consumer_app_id={appId}, file_type=0), so it goes to your Workshop showcase, not to Artwork.
steam.effect.featured: Reports each image as 1000 × 1 pixels (image_width, image_height), so Steam shows it as long artwork.
steam.effect.screenshot: Reports each image as 1000 × 1 pixels and marks it as a screenshot (file_type=5).
steam.batch.title: Upload many files at once
steam.batch.lead: Best for showcase parts: pick every GIF in one go.
steam.batch.step.button: Adds a “{button}” button to the top of the Steam page. Click it and select your GIFs.
steam.batch.step.order: Uploads the files in name order (part_01 first), waiting {seconds} s between uploads.
steam.batch.step.title: Gives each upload an invisible title, sets visibility to {visibility} and ticks Steam's rights checkbox.
steam.batch.step.direct: Sends the files straight to Steam with the sign-in from that tab. Nothing passes through Artwork Studio.
steam.batch.step.result: Skips files over 5 MB. When it finishes, the Console lists each file with its new item ID. For any FAILED file, reload the Steam page and run the script again with just those files.
steam.batch.done: Done: %ok uploaded, %failed not uploaded. Details are in the Console.
steam.batch.wrongPage: Open the Steam upload page (steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/edititem/767/3/) and run the script there.
steam.single.title: Fill in one upload form
steam.single.lead: For one file, when you'd rather click Save yourself.
steam.single.step.fill: Fills in an invisible title, sets visibility to Public and ticks Steam's rights checkbox.
steam.single.step.finish: Then choose your file and click Save and Continue. For the next file, reload the page and run it again.
steam.single.step.preview: If Steam's preview looks wrong, ignore it: Steam uploads the last file you selected.
steam.copyStatus: Copied. Paste it into the Console on the Steam upload page.
steam.copyFailed: Couldn't copy to the clipboard. Select the script below and copy it by hand.
steam.settings.title: Script settings
steam.settings.appId.note.workshop: Default: {appId}, which puts uploads in the Workshop showcase.
steam.settings.appId.note.other: Default: {appId}, the upload page's own app ID.
steam.settings.appId.invalid: Enter a whole number, such as 480.
steam.settings.visibility.note: Default: Public. Profile showcases only show items other people can see.
steam.settings.delay.note: Default: {seconds}. Shorter delays can make Steam refuse uploads.
steam.settings.invalid: Fix the highlighted setting to copy the script.
steam.footnote: Steam can change its upload page at any time. If a script stops working, <link>create a GitHub issue</link>.
guides.title: Guides
guides.intro: Step-by-step workflows for the common tasks in this toolkit.
guides.workshop.title: Workshop Showcase (5 parts)
guides.workshop.step1: Open Convert tab and keep preset as Workshop (5x150 slices).
guides.workshop.step3: Set GIF FPS and Min GIF FPS, or click Estimate for auto FPS.
guides.workshop.step4: Click Run Conversion and wait for Output ready in...
guides.workshop.step5: Review all 5 previews, then download single files or ZIP.
guides.workshop.tip: If quality drops, keep FPS reduction enabled so frame-rate changes are tried before Quality reduction. Workshop upload page: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/edititem/767/3/#
guides.featured.title: Featured Showcase (single wide)
guides.featured.step2: Upload source media (video, gif, png, webp, jpg, jpeg, bmp).
guides.featured.step3: Tune Featured Width and FPS if needed.
guides.featured.step4: Run conversion and check size/FPS/quality metadata under output.
guides.featured.step5: Download originalFileName_featured.gif directly or as part of ZIP.
guides.featured.tip: Start with lower FPS before increasing lossy settings for better visual quality. Artwork upload page: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/edititem/767/3/#
guides.showcase.title: Artwork Showcase (506 + 100)
guides.showcase.step1: Switch preset to Artwork Showcase (fixed 506px + 100px split).
guides.showcase.step2: Upload source media and tune FPS/size limits as needed.
guides.showcase.step3: Run conversion and verify both split outputs in preview.
guides.showcase.step4: Open Steam Helpers tab and copy either Artwork/Featured or Screenshot snippet (only one).
guides.showcase.step5: Run one snippet in Steam Console to prefill invisible title and agreement checkbox.
guides.showcase.tip: Use this flow only for the 506 + 100 showcase preset. Artwork/Screenshot upload page: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/edititem/767/3/#
guides.guide.title: Guide Artwork (195x195)
guides.guide.step2: Upload source media and keep the crop focused on the important area.
guides.guide.step3: Set GIF FPS if needed, or click Estimate to auto-fill a starting point.
guides.guide.step4: Run conversion and check the final size and FPS metadata under output.
guides.guide.step5: Download originalFileName_guide.gif and upload it on the Steam guide page.
guides.guide.tip: Guide uploads use the fixed 195x195 output. Guide upload page: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/editguide/?appid=760
guides.tuning.title: Fix size or quality issues
guides.tuning.step2: Set realistic Max GIF KB and Target GIF KB.
guides.tuning.step3: Leave standard retries off for speed-first behavior.
guides.tuning.step4: Enable standard retries if you want extra target-size chasing.
guides.tuning.step5: Use Worker Count 2-3 for speed, or 1 for stability debugging.
guides.tuning.tip: Current pipeline prioritizes FPS drops first and only reduces quality later if still oversize.
guides.patch.title: Patch existing files
guides.patch.step2: Use EOF Patch to rewrite last byte (default 0x21).
guides.patch.step3: Use GIF Header Patch to set logical width/height bytes.
guides.patch.step4: Optionally combine header + EOF in one run.
guides.patch.step5: Download patched outputs from the result list.
guides.steam.title: Steam upload autofill
guides.steam.step1: Open the Steam Helpers tab, choose what you're uploading and copy the batch or form script.
guides.steam.step2: Open the Steam upload page in your browser.
guides.steam.step3: Open the DevTools Console. The first time, type allow pasting and press Enter.
guides.steam.step4: Paste the script and press Enter.
guides.steam.step5: Pick your GIFs (batch) or your file (form), then check the result on Steam.
guides.steam.tip: Snippets are intended for Steam upload pages only. Use the matching upload URL from each section.
memoryDebug.title: Memory Debug
convert.runtime.optimizationsDisabled: Optimizations disabled: max-size checks and retry ladders are bypassed (raw encode mode).
convert.runtime.precheckEstimate: Precheck estimate: {estimatedKb}KB per GIF at {minGifFps}fps (allow {allowedKb}KB with margin).
convert.runtime.precheckBlocked: Precheck blocked conversion: estimated {estimatedKb}KB exceeds allowed {allowedKb}KB. Adjust limits/FPS or disable precheck.
convert.runtime.finishedEarlyWithOutputs: Finished early with {available}/{expected} output(s). Keeping completed outputs even if they exceed the target size.
convert.runtime.finishedEarlyWithoutOutp: Finished early before a complete output set was produced (0/{expected} output(s) available).
convert.runtime.oversizeOutputs: Some outputs still exceed max size ({maxGifKb}KB): {details}. Keeping outputs so you can preview/download anyway.
convert.runtime.workerCountCapped: Worker count capped to {count} for stability with wasm.
convert.error.unsupportedSource: Unsupported source file. Use a video file or image (.gif, .png, .webp, .jpg, .jpeg, .bmp).
